## Task: convert ONE Algebra 2 lesson packet from docx to LaTeX

You are working in `C:/Users/rober/Downloads/Projects/Lesson_planning`, a high-school
Algebra 2 lesson-planning toolchain. Each lesson has a Python builder
(`build_L{NN}_P{N}_packets.py`) that emits Word docx packets via python-docx.
We want to add a parallel LaTeX output path for camera-ready PDF rendering and
better visual graphing (TikZ/PGFPlots). This task is a single-lesson de-risking
pass; if it succeeds the same approach will be scaled to 17 other lessons.

### Lesson to convert: L41_P2 (Inverse Variation Applications + DOK-3 Performance Task)

### Inputs you must read before writing any code

1. `graph/eye_check/L41_P2.md` — **the structured intent brief**. It lists every
   anchor the LaTeX rewrite must preserve: callout titles + bodies, framework
   phase headers (DOK / minutes / teacher_does / students_do / questions /
   adult_role), sentence frames, bank-item labels and ordering, section ordering,
   visual requirements, and a "Must preserve / May restructure" contract at the
   bottom. **Treat this brief as the spec.**
2. `build_L41_P2_packets.py` — current source. Use only as a reference for the
   visual hierarchy. Do NOT modify it.
3. `L41_P2_Student_Packet.docx` — the canonical visual rendering. Open it if you
   can to compare your LaTeX output against.
4. `packet_styles.py` and `packet_build.py` — the docx-side primitives. Read
   `framework_phase_header`, `teal_section`, `sentence_frame_box`,
   `summary_exit_box`, `shade_cell`, `running_header_name_block`, `day_banner`
   so you understand what visual elements to recreate in LaTeX.
5. `questionbank/registry.jsonl` — the questionbank items. For L41_P2 you need
   the IDs listed in the `EXPLORE_IDS` / `REINFORCE_IDS` sections of the brief.
   Each row has `id`, `prompt`, `answers` (optional). Render `prompt` and
   `answers` exactly as text — don't paraphrase.

### Output (write only these files)

1. `tex/preamble.sty` — shared LaTeX style package. Define commands/environments
   for: callout (tcolorbox-based, parameterized title + color), section banner,
   framework_phase_header (a labeled box with DOK / minutes / teacher_does /
   students_do / questions / adult_role), sentence_frame_box, summary_exit_box,
   bank_item (label + prompt + answer choices). Use only standard CTAN packages
   (geometry, tcolorbox, fontspec/inputenc as appropriate, amsmath, pgfplots,
   tikz, enumitem, xcolor). The package will be reused by the other 17 lessons.
2. `tex/L41_P2_student.tex` — the L41_P2 student packet. Standalone document
   that compiles with `pdflatex tex/L41_P2_student.tex` (or lualatex/xelatex,
   pick whichever handles the unicode best — there are em-dashes, smart quotes,
   curly quotes, and the ⭐ / 🎯 / ⚠️ / 📘 / 📌 / 🔭 / 🕐 / 🧩 / 🌍 emojis used in
   callout titles. If emojis won't render, replace with text equivalents like
   `[STAR]`, `[FOCUS]`, `[WARN]` and document the substitution at the top of
   `preamble.sty`.).

Do NOT produce do_now or teacher packets in this task — student packet only.

### Must preserve (from the brief's contract — non-negotiable)

- All callout titles AND body lines verbatim. These are "rules printed on the
  page" and ELL-supports; teachers and evaluators look for them.
- Sentence frames verbatim — ELL non-negotiable.
- Bank-item ordering and labels exactly as listed in the brief's
  "Bank-item labels (in order)" section.
- Section ordering: Launch → Explore → Share/Summary → Exit → (back) Optional Reinforcement.
- The `📘 APPLICATION RULES` and `⚠️ DIRECT vs INVERSE` callouts at the top of
  the Launch section must remain visually prominent (color-coded, bordered,
  page-anchored — NOT flowed inline as plain paragraphs).

### May restructure (your call)

- Margin sizes, font choices, table styling — match the docx visual hierarchy
  but use LaTeX-native idioms. Don't try to match docx pixel-for-pixel.
- Color hex values — use the closest equivalent in xcolor's named palette OR
  define them via `\definecolor` from the hex. Either is fine.
- The objectives + framework header tables can render as `tabular`, `longtable`,
  `tcolorbox`-based, or even a labeled list — preserve the content, choose
  the presentation.

### Validation pass before reporting done

1. Run `pdflatex tex/L41_P2_student.tex` (or `lualatex` if pdflatex chokes on
   unicode). Resolve any errors. Re-run if needed for refs.
2. Confirm a PDF was produced. Report the page count.
3. Open the PDF (or extract text via `pdftotext`) and verify by sampling:
   - The "📘 APPLICATION RULES" callout body matches the brief verbatim.
   - The "Pair share (Ramón task)" sentence frame matches verbatim.
   - All 5 EXPLORE bank items appear with their labeled headers.
   - The "🔭 BRIDGE TO P3 (Wednesday)" callout appears.
4. Write a short summary at the end of your response covering:
   - Which LaTeX engine you used (pdflatex / lualatex / xelatex) and why.
   - Any anchor you couldn't preserve and why.
   - Any color-hex substitutions you made.
   - Any emoji substitutions you made.
   - The PDF file path and page count.
   - Suggested follow-ups for scaling to the other 17 lessons.

### Constraints

- Write ONLY to `tex/`. Do not modify any existing Python or docx files.
- Do not run `npx gitnexus`, do not commit, do not push. The orchestrator will
  review and commit.
- If you can't open the docx file (no parser available), don't sweat it — the
  brief is the spec; the docx is a reference rendering for human comparison
  later.
- Hard timeout is 600s. If you hit time pressure, prioritize: (1) preamble.sty
  compiles, (2) student.tex compiles to a PDF, (3) all callouts present, (4)
  visual polish. Skip (4) if needed.
